newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO to rule on US-EC computer tariff dispute.
newsitem.headline: WTO to rule on US-EC computer tariff dispute.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) set up a neutral panel to rule on a U.S. complaint against the European Community for its customs reclassification of certain computer equipment, a WTO spokesman said.

The reclassification for tariff purpose covers certain Local Area Network (LAN) adapter equipment and personal computers with multimedia capability, which Washington alleges has resulted in higher duties being imposed on U.S. imports.
The U.S. trade delegation took the floor to say that the EC's reclassification of LAN adapter cards begun in mid-1995 had affected hundreds of millions of dollars in U.S. exports.

EC tariffs on such products -- which include hubs, in-line repeaters, converters, bridges and routers -- rose from 3.5 percent as automatic data processing machines to 7.5 percent as telecommunications apparatus, according to the U.S. complaint.
India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore reserved their rights as third parties to the dispute, according to trade sources at the WTO's closed-door Dispute Settlement Body.
